source_grounding.call_chain_traced: actix delete_collection (src/actix/api/collections_api.rs:161) -> dispatcher.submit_collection_meta_op(CollectionMetaOperations::DeleteCollection(name)) -> TableOfContent::perform_collection_meta_op (lib/storage/src/content_manager/toc/collection_meta_ops.rs:78) -> TableOfContent::delete_collection (toc/collection_meta_ops.rs:211): collections.remove(name) returns None for a never-created name and collection_path does not exist -> result=false (line 284) -> Ok(false) -> actix process_response (src/actix/helpers.rs:52) maps every Ok(_) to HttpResponse::Ok() (HTTP 200) with result field -> observed {"result":false,"status":"ok"}. No code path on this route emits StorageError::NotFound. Contrast on the read face of the same resource: do_get_collection raises CollectionError::NotFound -> StorageError::NotFound (lib/storage/src/content_manager/errors.rs:20,130) -> src/actix/helpers.rs:246 maps to 404, matching the observed GET 404 in output_state_collections_delete_005.log. gRPC face (src/tonic/api/collections_api.rs:116-122) submits the identical meta op via perform_operation, so the same Ok(bool) disposition applies there (not exercised at runtime — face_unavailable).
source_grounding.outcome_note: The source performs no existence validation on the DELETE route that could yield the contract-required 404: the missing-collection branch is coded as Ok(false) and the REST layer unconditionally maps Ok to 200. No explicit intent marker (no 'intentionally'/'by design'/'we don't guarantee' comment or maintainer citation) exists on this branch — the only comments (toc/collection_meta_ops.rs:273-274, 241-245) address the create-lock and busy-collection cleanup, not the API disposition — so by_design_in_source is not available under the tightened v3.4 rule; the unannotated idempotence hypothesis is left to the auditor via mundane_explanation.surviving.

mundane_explanation.surviving: unannotated intended idempotence: the OpenAPI-documented envelope boolean (result: boolean) is the only designed non-existence signal, so a maintainer may argue delete is deliberately idempotent; however no explicit intent evidence (comment/docstring/maintainer citation) marks the 200-for-missing disposition as deliberate, so this hypothesis cannot be confirmed from source and is left for the auditor
